chunks: And We followed them in this world with a curse, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be of the despised.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean to be among the 'maqboheen' on the Day of Resurrection?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the dual nature of divine retribution, where the 'curse' (la'nah) in this world signifies the removal of divine mercy and the 'disgrace' (maqboheen) in the Hereafter denotes eternal rejection. It is frequently interpreted as applying to the followers of Pharaoh, illustrating how their persistent arrogance led to a complete severance from God's grace both temporally and eternally.
